key_insight: A high-Reynolds-number asymptotic theory reveals that hypersonic blunt-body boundary layers first amplify streamwise vorticity through a slow-down convection mechanism near the nose, then produce strong downstream transient growth via lift-up.
engineering_relevance: These receptivity mechanisms help predict and control disturbance amplification in hypersonic boundary layers, which is important for transition, heating, and vehicle design.
method: High-Reynolds-number asymptotic analysis of receptivity in the nose region.
Reduced-order model for downstream evolution of non-modal perturbations.
Comparison against SF-HLNS numerical simulations for validation.
evidence_signal: The reduced model is reported to agree well with SF-HLNS calculations across the studied regime.
watch_item: The theory is asymptotic and tied to high-Reynolds-number hypersonic blunt-body conditions, so accuracy may degrade outside that regime or for different geometries.
paper_title: Excitation of non-modal perturbations in hypersonic boundary layers by free stream forcing. Part II: asymptotic theory and key mechanisms
